q: In a circular motion, the object just moves in a ____.
e: Circular motion is defined by an object traveling along a circular path.

q: In rotational motion, the object rotates about an ____.
e: Rotational motion involves an object spinning around a central axis.

q: A rigid body is a body that does not ____ or change shape.
e: A rigid body maintains its physical shape under motion or force.

q: In a rigid body, no matter how the body moves, the ____ between any two particles within the body remains constant.
e: The internal distances between particles in a rigid body do not change.

q: If a rigid body is in rotational motion, all the particles constituting it undergo circular motion about a common ____.
e: Every particle in a rotating rigid body moves in a circle around the same axis of rotation.

q: When an object (rigid body) rotates, it can speed up (or) ____ down.
e: Rotating objects can experience changes in their rotational speed.

q: During the time intervals when an object speeds up or slows down, its angular velocity is changing therefore it has an angular ____.
e: A change in angular velocity over time results in angular acceleration.

q: If the angular velocity changes at a constant rate, the angular acceleration is ____.
e: A uniform rate of change in angular velocity means the angular acceleration does not vary.

q: Rotational variables include angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular ____.
e: These three variables are the primary parameters used to describe rotational kinematics.

q: The kinematic equations for rotational motion are derived for an object that rotates with a constant angular ____.
e: The standard rotational kinematic equations assume constant angular acceleration.

q: The magnitude of angular velocity of the object at $t=0$ is called the initial angular ____.
e: Initial angular speed represents how fast the object is rotating at the start of the time interval.

q: The formula for average angular speed is $\omega = \frac{\omega + \omega_0}{____}$.
e: Average angular speed is the arithmetic mean of the initial and final angular speeds.

q: The equations of motion for constant angular acceleration are analogous to equations for constant acceleration in ____ motion.
e: Rotational kinematic equations mirror linear kinematic equations by substituting angular variables for linear ones.

q: In Grade 10, kinematic equations were derived for linear motion with constant ____.
e: Linear kinematic equations apply to objects moving in a straight line with unchanging acceleration.

q: In the analogy between linear and angular motion, linear velocity $v$ corresponds to angular velocity $\____$.
e: Angular velocity $\omega$ is the rotational equivalent of linear velocity $v$.

q: In the kinematic analogies, linear displacement $s$ corresponds to angular displacement $\____$.
e: Angular displacement $\theta$ measures the angle rotated, analogous to linear distance $s$.

q: The linear equation $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2as$ is analogous to the angular equation $\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 + 2\alpha\____$.
e: Angular displacement $\theta$ replaces linear displacement $s$ in this time-independent kinematic equation.

q: In the analogy of kinematic equations, linear acceleration $a$ corresponds to angular acceleration $\____$.
e: Angular acceleration $\alpha$ is the rate of change of angular velocity, matching linear acceleration $a$.

q: The linear equation $s = \frac{v + v_0}{2} t$ corresponds to the angular equation $\theta = \frac{\omega + \omega_0}{____} t$.
e: Both equations calculate displacement using the average velocity or angular velocity multiplied by time.

q: According to the summary, angular acceleration is constant if the angular velocity changes at a constant ____.
e: A steady rate of change in angular velocity defines constant angular acceleration.

q: Motion with a constant rate of change of angular velocity is called rotational motion under constant angular ____.
e: This specific type of motion allows the use of standard rotational kinematic equations.

q: The summary states that for uniform circular motion, the centripetal acceleration vector points towards the ____ of the circular path.
e: Centripetal acceleration is always directed inward toward the center of the circle.

q: The summary notes that the linear velocity vector is ____ to the circular path.
e: Linear velocity is always directed along the tangent to the circular path at any given point.

q: The acceleration directed towards the centre of the circular path is called ____ acceleration.
e: Centripetal means 'center-seeking', describing the direction of this acceleration.

q: The angular acceleration is equal to ____ when there is no change in angular velocity.
e: If angular velocity is constant, its rate of change (angular acceleration) is zero.

q: The relations between linear quantities and ____ quantities for circular motion were studied in Grade 11.
e: Physics connects linear motion parameters to their angular counterparts in rotational systems.

q: All particles of an object rotating around the axis of rotation move in a ____ path.
e: Every individual particle in a rotating rigid body traces a circular trajectory.

q: All particles of a rotating body move in a circle lying on a plane that is ____ to the axis.
e: The circular paths of particles are situated in planes that cross the axis of rotation at right angles.

q: For particles in rotational motion, the centre of rotation lies on the ____.
e: The center of every circular particle path is located on the main axis of rotation.

q: The relation between arc length $s$ and angular displacement $\theta$ is $s = \____ \theta$.
e: Arc length equals the radius multiplied by the angular displacement in radians.

q: In the equation $s = r \theta$, the variable $r$ represents the ____ of the circle.
e: The radius is the distance from the axis of rotation to the particle.

q: The instantaneous angular velocity $\omega$ of a rotational object is the ____ for all the particles comprising the object.
e: While linear speeds vary by radius, all particles in a rigid body share the exact same angular velocity.

q: The magnitude of the linear velocity $v$ is related to the angular velocity $\omega$ by the equation $v = \____ \omega$.
e: Linear velocity increases proportionally with the distance from the axis of rotation.

q: Because its direction is tangent to the path, linear velocity is also called ____ velocity.
e: Tangential velocity describes the linear speed and direction of a particle along the edge of the circular path.

q: If the magnitude of the angular velocity changes, the object will have a ____ acceleration.
e: A change in the magnitude of velocity (speed) along the circular path results in tangential acceleration.

q: The direction of tangential acceleration is always ____ to the circular path.
e: Tangential acceleration acts along the tangent line, either speeding up or slowing down the particle.

q: The tangential acceleration $a_T$ relates to angular acceleration $\alpha$ by the equation $a_T = \____ \alpha$.
e: Tangential acceleration is the product of the radius and the angular acceleration.

q: Tangential acceleration is a measure of how fast the tangential ____ changes.
e: It specifically quantifies the rate of change of the particle's linear speed along the path.

q: The direction of the angular velocity vector is ____ to the plane of rotation.
e: Angular velocity is a vector that points along the axis of rotation, perpendicular to the plane in which the object spins.

q: The direction of the angular velocity vector is usually specified by the ____-hand rule.
e: The right-hand rule is the standard convention for determining the direction of rotational vectors.

q: In the right-hand rule, the fingers are wrapped to point in the direction of ____.
e: Curling the fingers mimics the circular path of the rotating object.

q: In the right-hand rule, the ____ points in the direction of the angular velocity vector.
e: The extended thumb indicates the orientation of the angular velocity vector along the axis.

q: When the angular velocity is increasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the ____ direction as the angular velocity.
e: If an object is spinning faster, angular acceleration and angular velocity share the same vector direction.

q: When the angular velocity is decreasing, the angular acceleration vector points ____ to the angular velocity.
e: If an object is slowing down, the angular acceleration vector opposes the direction of angular velocity.

q: Angular acceleration $\alpha$ is measured in radian per second ____.
e: The standard SI unit for angular acceleration is radians per second squared ($rad/s^2$).

q: Table 1.2 expresses the relation between linear and ____ quantities.
e: The table maps linear kinematic variables to their rotational equivalents.

q: The text uses a randomly shaped ____ body to illustrate rotational motion.
e: A rigid body is used because its fixed internal distances make rotational kinematics predictable.

q: All particles comprising a rotating rigid body share the same instantaneous angular ____.
e: Regardless of their distance from the axis, all particles complete a full rotation in the same amount of time.

q: The relation $v = r \omega$ applies to ____ particle of the rotational object.
e: This fundamental equation links linear and angular speed for any given particle in the rigid body.

q: A change in the magnitude of angular velocity causes the magnitude of linear velocity to ____.
e: Since $v = r \omega$ and $r$ is constant for a specific particle, changing $\omega$ directly changes $v$.

q: An object that moves in a circle at constant speed is said to experience ____ circular motion.
e: Uniform circular motion is defined by a constant linear speed along the circular path.

q: In uniform circular motion, the magnitude of the velocity remains constant, but the ____ of the velocity continuously changes.
e: Velocity is a vector; even if speed is constant, the continuous change in direction means velocity is changing.

q: The continuous change in the direction of velocity constitutes an ____.
e: Any change in velocity, whether in magnitude or direction, requires an acceleration.

q: An object revolving in a circle is continuously accelerated, even when its ____ remains constant.
e: The change in direction alone is sufficient to produce continuous acceleration.

q: Average acceleration is defined as the change in velocity divided by the change in ____.
e: The formula for average acceleration is $a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$.

q: Instantaneous acceleration is obtained when the time interval $\Delta t$ approaches ____.
e: Taking the limit as $\Delta t \to 0$ yields the exact acceleration at a specific instant.

q: During the time interval $\Delta t$, the object covers a distance along the ____ which subtends an angle $\Delta \theta$.
e: The path traveled along the circumference is referred to as the arc length.

q: As $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the angular displacement $\Delta \theta$ becomes very ____.
e: An infinitesimally small time interval results in an infinitesimally small change in angle.

q: When $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the change in velocity $\Delta v$ is essentially ____ to the velocity vectors.
e: In uniform circular motion, the infinitesimal change in velocity points directly inward, perpendicular to the tangential velocity.

q: The instantaneous acceleration in uniform circular motion points toward the ____ of the circle.
e: This inward-pointing acceleration is responsible for continuously turning the object's velocity vector.

q: Acceleration directed toward the centre of a circular path is called ____ acceleration.
e: Centripetal acceleration maintains the circular trajectory by pulling the object inward.

q: Centripetal acceleration is also called radial acceleration because it is directed along the ____.
e: The acceleration vector lies exactly on the radial line connecting the object to the center.

q: The derivation of centripetal acceleration uses the fact that the position triangle is geometrically ____ to the velocity vector triangle.
e: Geometric similarity between the displacement and velocity triangles allows the ratio of sides to be equated.

q: In uniform circular motion, the magnitudes of initial and final velocities are equal, so $v_1 = v_2 = \____$.
e: Because speed is constant, the length of the velocity vectors remains $v$.

q: As $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the relation becomes $\Delta v = \frac{v}{\____} \Delta s$.
e: This proportionality comes from the similar triangles relating velocity change to arc length.

q: Centripetal acceleration is defined as the limit of $\frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$ as $\Delta t$ approaches ____.
e: This limit defines the exact instantaneous centripetal acceleration.

q: The limit of $\frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}$ as $\Delta t \to 0$ represents the linear ____ of the object.
e: The rate of change of arc length with respect to time is the linear speed $v$.

q: The formula for centripetal acceleration in terms of linear speed is $a_c = \frac{\____^2}{r}$.
e: This is the standard equation for calculating centripetal acceleration using linear speed and radius.

q: Substituting $v = r \omega$ into the centripetal acceleration formula yields $a_c = r \____^2$.
e: This alternative form calculates centripetal acceleration using angular velocity and radius.

q: In uniform circular motion, the linear velocity vector is ____ to the path.
e: Linear velocity always points along the tangent line to the circle at the object's location.

q: At every point in the path of uniform circular motion, centripetal acceleration and linear velocity are ____ to each other.
e: The radial acceleration and tangential velocity form a 90-degree angle.

q: Nonuniform circular motion is characterized by a varying ____.
e: Unlike uniform circular motion, the object's linear speed changes over time.

q: A varying linear speed in circular motion means the angular ____ is changing.
e: Since $v = r \omega$, a change in linear speed directly implies a change in angular speed.

q: Angular acceleration in nonuniform circular motion gives rise to ____ acceleration.
e: Tangential acceleration is responsible for increasing or decreasing the object's speed along the path.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, tangential acceleration exists in addition to ____ acceleration.
e: The object still requires centripetal acceleration to maintain its circular path while its speed changes.

q: The resultant acceleration in nonuniform circular motion is the vector ____ of centripetal and tangential accelerations.
e: The total acceleration vector is found by adding the radial and tangential components.

q: Unlike tangential acceleration, ____ acceleration is present in both uniform and nonuniform circular motion.
e: Any circular motion requires centripetal acceleration to bend the path into a circle.

q: The vectors for centripetal acceleration and tangential acceleration are ____ to each other.
e: One acts radially inward, while the other acts tangentially along the edge, creating a 90-degree angle.

q: The centripetal acceleration vector $a_c$ acts in the ____ direction.
e: Radial refers to the direction along the radius, pointing toward the center.

q: The tangential acceleration vector $a_T$ acts in the ____ direction.
e: Tangential refers to the direction tangent to the circular path.

q: The resultant acceleration vector points at an ____ between $a_c$ and $a_T$.
e: Because it is the vector sum of two perpendicular components, the total acceleration points diagonally inward.

q: The magnitude of the resultant acceleration is found using the formula $a = \sqrt{a_c^2 + \____^2}$.
e: This applies the Pythagorean theorem to the perpendicular radial and tangential acceleration components.

q: The direction of the resultant acceleration vector is given by the equation $\tan \theta = \frac{\____}{a_c}$.
e: This trigonometric ratio determines the angle of the total acceleration vector relative to the radial direction.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, the object experiences tangential acceleration which is ____ to the circle.
e: This acceleration component lies exactly on the tangent line of the circular path.

q: Thus, an object in nonuniform circular motion has a resultant acceleration that is the vector sum of the centripetal and ____ accelerations.
e: The total acceleration accounts for both the turning of the object and its changing speed.
